report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true**. Strong clinical trial evidence confirms that two doses of the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, marketed as Shingrix) significantly reduce the incidence of shingles (herpes zoster) and its complications in adults aged 70 years or older.

### Evidence Summary
* **High Efficacy in Older Adults:** In the pivotal Phase III clinical trial (ZOE-70), RZV demonstrated approximately 90% efficacy in preventing herpes zoster among participants aged 70 years and older.
* **Reduction in Complications:** The vaccine substantially lowers the risk of postherpetic neuralgia (PHN), a frequent and severe nerve pain condition that can follow shingles in older individuals.
* **Sustained Protection:** Long-term follow-up extension studies (ZOE-LTFU) show that high vaccine efficacy and immune responses remain durable for up to 6–11 years post-vaccination in adults aged 70+.
* **Public Health Guidance:** Public health bodies, such as the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), recommend RZV as the preferred vaccine for preventing shingles in adults aged 50 and older due to its high performance regardless of advancing age.

### Sources
* CDC Shingles Vaccination: https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/vaccines/index.html
* PubMed - Long-Term Protection of RZV: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34283213/
* PubMed Central - Recombinant Zoster Vaccine Review: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7336348/
* Immunisation Advisory Centre - Shingrix: https://immune.org.nz/vaccine/shingrix
